provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

provisions.title: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
provisions.text: The Secure attribute for sensitive cookies in HTTPS sessions is not set.

provisions.title: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
provisions.text: The product generates a hash for a password, but it uses a scheme that does not provide a sufficient level of computational effort that would make password cracking attacks infeasible or expensive.

negative

value.reason: The route `GET /rest/memories` in server.ts:670 is registered with no authorization middleware, so anyone can call it. Its handler in routes/memory.ts:24 runs `MemoryModel.findAll({ include: [UserModel] })` without an `attributes` allow-list or exclusion, so every column of the linked User record is loaded. Per models/user.ts, that record holds email, the password hash, role, lastLoginIp, profileImage and several other redacted fields that are likely secrets or tokens. Only the username and email setters do any sanitizing, and none of the fields are hidden from serialization. This matches the positive SEC-07 example: an unauthenticated list endpoint that returns memories with the full nested user records, exposing sensitive object properties. The supplied Evidence does not show the `res.json` call, but the handler's name and route make it clear the result is returned to the client.
